headline: Knowledge networks are scaffolding annotation and interpretation of omics data
label: Network Guided Biomedical Knowledge
summary: Public omics resources and metabolomics tools are increasingly built around explicit network or knowledge-graph structure to make annotations traceable.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit network or knowledge-graph structure as the scaffold for interpreting heterogeneous omics data. NLM-CKN links single-cell-derived cell phenotypes across 88 datasets and 10 human organs to Cell Ontology terms, genes, diseases and drugs, forming a semantic network that can be traversed from phenotype to therapeutic context. FeatureMAP applies network guidance to untargeted LC-MS, pairing metabolite annotation with module discovery over the PhenoMAP knowledge graph. What is new relative to network-conditioned prediction is the emphasis on the network as a reusable resource for annotation and traceability rather than only a model constraint. TRACE addresses provenance in public omics curation, demonstrated on a harmonised single-cell glaucoma resource, while Met-SC offers a metabolomics database with standardized deposition, spectral libraries and 27 online analysis tools. These two focus on resource construction rather than network-guided inference, so they extend the thread rather than fully share it.
